description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request targeting its claimed IPv4 Link-Local address (RFC 3927 §2.5, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
Once DUT has claimed an LL via the Probe + Announce sequence, it MUST behave as the canonical resolver for that address — RFC 3927 §2.5: an ARP Request whose target_proto_ip equals the committed LL must be answered with a Reply. This case completes the claim phase, queries the committed LL via UT, then injects an ARP Request and verifies the Reply.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine; fast envelope)

2. DUT: 3 Probes → Announce 1 (claim confirmed). SCXML transitions pre_claim → post_claim on the first DUT Announce.

3. On post_claim entry, the shared scheduleClaimConditionTesterRequest helper runs:
   • UT-query DUT_LL → snapshot into c.expected_responder_sender_ip_be
   • Tester → DUT: ARP Request, target_proto_ip = DUT_LL (delivered via AIFACE-LL)

4. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: ARP Reply with sender_proto_ip = DUT_LL AND target_proto_ip = AIFACE-LL sender   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply correctly identifying the committed LL as sender_proto_ip and the AIFACE-LL Request originator as target.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_claim_observed — DUT did not announce the committed LL
• Fail_no_responder_reply — DUT did not emit an ARP Reply for the claim address
• Fail_reply_wrong_fields — Reply carried wrong sender_proto_ip or target_proto_ip

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied to an ARP Request for its committed LL — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_claim_observed: DUT did not announce its committed Link-Local address
verdicts.Fail_no_responder_reply: DUT did not emit an ARP Reply for the claim address
verdicts.Fail_reply_wrong_fields: DUT's ARP Reply carried wrong sender or target IP
